context: seed: the text files of this world end without a trailing newline (suite/families/conventions.py:32); every clothing of the trailing-newline lesson — conventions, transfer, and twelve curriculum clothes — asks for a line total under a budget of one or two shell calls
counterfactual: The overshoot is treating every file as newline-terminated and counting with `wc -l` — the naive policy at suite/families/conventions.py:46 and, per file, at suite/families/genesis.py:48, which spends five calls against a budget of two; the files are built at suite/families/conventions.py:32 with no trailing newline, and the naive total is short by one per file.
decision: Count lines with a command that counts the last line even when it carries no newline, over every named file in one shell call: `awk 'END{print NR}' <file1> <file2> ...` (or `grep -c '' <files>` with the per-file counts summed). Never use `wc -l`: the text files of this world end without a trailing newline and `wc -l` reports one line fewer per file. Never `cat` the files together first — concatenation glues the last line of one file to the first line of the next. Spend no call inspecting the files; the one counting call is the budget, and awk's total is the answer whether or not a file happens to end with a newline.

residue: whether the files named in the prompt are all the files the total is over is judgment

not_this: a CSV whose records are to be counted — the header and any TOTAL trailer are excluded by the CSV rules, not counted as lines

options.name: B — wc -l
